digest.en: Estonia is closing its remaining road border crossings with Russia, citing escalating hybrid threats. Simultaneously, leaked data reveals over 300 Russian soldiers killed while propping up Mali’s junta. These moves signal a hardening front across both European and African theaters.
digest.hi: Mississippi के Horn Island के पास एक निजी जेट समुद्र में गिरा, दो बच्चों सहित छह लोग लापता, बचाव दल अभी भी खोज जारी रखे हैं। इसी दौरान मध्य पूर्व में हमले की संभावना बढ़ी, अमेरिकी दूतावास ने अपने नागरिकों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी।

articles.title: Contrer la menace du Jnim sur les centres urbains du Sahel
articles.summary: Al-Qaeda in the Sahel has intensified attacks on urban centers. Military responses risk worsening the human toll. Negotiated solutions may offer a less damaging path forward for the region. Ces dernières années, la branche d’al-Qaeda au Sahel a multiplié les assauts contre les villes de la région. Chercher à vaincre les jihadistes par les armes ne ferait qu’alourdir un bilan humain déjà considérable.

articles.title: Questions sur un retour en force
articles.summary: Crisis Group analysts discussed the deployment of Algerian troops in Niger. They examined how this military presence affects regional security balances. The conversation highlighted shifting dynamics in the Sahel. Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Ibrahim Yahaya Ibrahim, Directeur Adjoint du Projet Sahel, Ibrahim Maïga, Conseiller Spécial pour le Sahel et Michaël Ayari, Analyste Senior pour la Tunisie et l’Algérie à Crisis Group, pour parler du déploiement de troupes algériennes au Niger et des répercussions de cette présence militaire sur les équilibres sécuritaires.

articles.title: Trump awards Rudy Giuliani the Medal of Freedom
articles.summary: Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Giuliani gained prominence after the 9/11 attacks and ran for president in 2007. He remained a key conservative figure despite his failed bid. The honor reflects his enduring political influence. After the 9/11 attacks, Mr. Giuliani ‌became one of the most popular figures in U. S. politics. He launched a Republican presidential ‌bid ⁠in 2007, and even after it failed, he remained a prominent conservative ⁠messenger.

articles.title: Tech firms back in crosshairs as Huang rally reverses
articles.summary: Asian tech stocks fell in Taipei, Tokyo, and Seoul. This reversal followed a previous surge driven by Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO. The region hosts most key AI-linked firms. Investors reacted negatively to the recent market volatility. Taipei, Tokyo and Seoul - home of most of the region's key AI-linked firms - were all down, a day after a surge on the back of the news of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

articles.title: Estonia warns of growing Russian hybrid threats, to close remaining road border crossings
articles.summary: Estonia will close road border crossings with Russia from December 1. The closure lasts at least six months due to security concerns. Tallinn accused Moscow of orchestrating two arson attacks on defense companies this year. The move highlights growing hybrid threats. Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia from Dec 1 for at least six months, citing security concerns after accusing Moscow of orchestrating two attempted arson attacks on its defence companies this year.

articles.title: China investigates politburo star in Xi Jinping’s latest purge
articles.summary: China launched an investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining. He is a member of the elite politburo. This marks the fourth top leader investigated since 2025. Chen was considered a contender for higher office before the probe began. articles.title: Taliban Pressures Afghan Men To Enforce Restrictions On Their Wives And Daughters
articles.summary: Taliban authorities pressure Afghan men to restrict their female family members. Men are told to forbid women from leaving home or withhold cell phones. These measures enforce strict gender segregation. The regime uses male relatives as enforcers. Afghan men and women have told RFE/RL's Radio Azadi that Afghanistan's Taliban authorities are making men impose strict restrictions on female family members, such as forbidding them to leave the home or withholding cell phones.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary: Leaked records show 349 Russian military personnel died in Mali over three years. The data highlights Moscow’s support for the local junta. The figures also reveal broader Russian military activity across the African continent during the same period. Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in AfricaWhen the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard.

articles.title: Concern for trapped Ebola workers as violence against women and girls deepens
articles.summary: WHO staff and Ebola responders remain trapped in a DRC hospital. Heavy fighting continues in Ituri province. The UN agency confirmed the situation on Tuesday. Personnel are stranded as violence prevents their safe evacuation from the facility. Staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and Ebola responders remain trapped in a hospital in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as heavy fighting continues in the vicinity, the UN agency said in an update on Tuesday.

articles.title: Guterres urges renewed commitment to landmark peace deal
articles.summary: Guterres praised Colombia for progress since the Final Peace Agreement. The accord ended over fifty years of insurgency. He stressed the need for full implementation of its provisions. The UN chief urged renewed commitment to the landmark deal. UN Secretary-General António Guterres has commended Colombia for progress achieved in the decade since a landmark accord known as the Final Peace Agreement ended more than 50 years of insurgency but stressed the need to fully implement its provisions.

articles.title: UN deputy chief’s final call to end violence against women
articles.summary: Amina Mohammed warned another woman would be killed before she finished speaking. She called for justice for survivors and consequences for perpetrators. The UN deputy chief made this final plea to end violence against women and girls. UN deputy chief’s final call to end violence against women.

articles.title: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?
articles.summary: The Security Council is weighing how AI and drones reshape warfare. Guterres noted these technologies are fuelling record conflict levels. Disinformation spreads rapidly, complicating peace efforts. The UN is assessing how to keep pace with these changes. When the UN was founded in 1945, computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is already assisting in targeting, drones are reshaping warfare and disinformation is spreading in unprecedented ways, fuelling record levels of conflict.

articles.title: Huang’s comeback won’t ease Southeast Asia’s data center crunch
articles.summary: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia chief executive after a board vote. Nvidia shares rose over 31 percent in New York. Southeast Asia still faces a severe data center shortage despite the stock rally. Monday’s unanimous board vote reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive, backed publicly by US President Donald Trump, triggered a sharp relief rally across global artificial intelligence stocks, with Nvidia shares surging more than 31% in New York trading.

articles.title: Asia rescues markets, Trump rescues Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Asian governments banned short sales and deployed state funds to stabilize markets after a global selloff hit the artificial intelligence sector. Seoul, Taipei, and Beijing acted to prevent a tech rout from spreading. Trump also intervened to support Jensen Huang during the downturn. NEW YORK – When a brutal global selloff wiped trillions of dollars off the artificial intelligence trade, Asia’s policymakers did what they always do: they reached deep into their crisis playbooks.

articles.title: Barbados town’s three-year deal with Bristol ‘part of the reparative process’
articles.summary: Speightstown in Barbados signed a three-year twinning agreement with Bristol, United Kingdom. Labour minister Colin Jordan stated the deal acknowledges the historical links between the two places. The partnership is described as part of a broader reparative process regarding the transatlantic slave trade. articles.title: Jensen Huang’s return locks Nvidia deeper into US statecraft
articles.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his resignation. Shares surged roughly thirty percent in New York trading. Investors priced in product roadmap continuity, treating the reversal as an immediate restoration of the status quo. When Nvidia’s board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive less than two weeks after his resignation, equity markets treated the reversal as an immediate restoration of the status quo.

articles.title: Gaza war has undone 77 years of human development, UN warns
articles.summary: The UN deputy chief warned that the Gaza war has undone seventy-seven years of human development. Palestinians face violence and displacement despite the October 2025 ceasefire. He urged renewed international support for a two-state solution to the conflict. The UN deputy chief urged renewed international support for a two-State solution to the Israel-Palestine conflict on Monday, warning that Palestinians continue to face violence, displacement and dire living conditions despite the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.

articles.title: UN chief urges talks on global AI safety framework, warns of historic shift in power
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for talks on a multilateral AI safety framework. He warned that artificial intelligence is driving the biggest transfer of power in human history. Member States must begin discussions to manage these emerging technological risks. UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Monday called on Member States to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence (AI), warning that the technology is driving “the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind”.

articles.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Warship, Cargo Vessel Off Libya's Coast
articles.summary: Ukraine struck a Russian corvette and a cargo ship near Benghazi, Libya. Seven Ukrainian-made sea drones executed the operation. The corvette carried a Ka-27 helicopter. The cargo vessel allegedly transported weapons across the Mediterranean Sea. Kyiv confirmed the details of the attack. Ukraine says that it struck a Russian corvette carrying a Ka-27 helicopter near the port of Benghazi, Libya, as well as a cargo ship allegedly used to transport weapons across the Mediterranean Sea.

articles.title: Why Taiwanese firms resist leaving China, even as tensions rise
articles.summary: Acer and Asus are relocating production lines from Thailand and Vietnam back to mainland China. The move counters rising geopolitical tensions and leverages established supply chains. Stan Shih represented Taiwan at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The shift highlights the economic pull of the Chinese market despite political friction. When Stan Shih, the founder of electronics company Acer, arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen to represent Taiwan at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit recently, his company was already in the news.

articles.title: NATO-Like Guarantees For Ukraine? US Envoy Signals Possibility, But Questions Remain
articles.summary: Jared Kushner said Donald Trump might offer Ukraine security guarantees modeled on NATO commitments. This possibility hinges on reducing the risk of another Russian invasion. The envoy signaled this potential shift on November 22. Questions remain regarding the specific terms and conditions of such an arrangement. US President Donald Trump may consider offering Ukraine security guarantees modeled on NATO's collective-defense commitments if he is convinced that the risk of another Russian invasion has been sufficiently reduced, special envoy Jared Kushner said on November 22.

articles.title: Rescuers Search For Victims After Russia Attacks Apartment Building Near Kyiv
articles.summary: Russian drones destroyed a residential building in Dymer, 45 kilometers north of Kyiv. At least five people died, including an 18-year-old man. Rescuers searched for survivors and other victims. The attack targeted a civilian area near the capital. At least five people were confirmed dead after Russian drone strikes destroyed a residential building in the town of Dymer, about 45 kilometers north of Kyiv.

articles.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’
articles.summary: COP31 concluded without a binding climate agreement. Negotiators failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuel phaseouts. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the outcome deeply disappointing. The two-week summit ended with no new commitments to accelerate global emissions reductions. COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.

articles.title: Guterres laments COP31 outcome, urges climate justice from Barbados
articles.summary: António Guterres expressed disappointment over the collapse of COP31 climate negotiations during a visit to Barbados. He urged stronger action on fossil fuels, climate finance, and support for vulnerable nations. The Secretary-General called for climate justice as the talks failed to reach a consensus. Secretary-General António Guterres on Sunday expressed deep disappointment over the collapse of COP31 climate negotiations, using a visit to Barbados to call for stronger action on fossil fuels, climate finance and support for vulnerable nations.

articles.summary: केपीएमजी और सीआईआई की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार 93 प्रतिशत भारतीय कंपनियां एआई एजेंट्स अपनाने के लिए तैयार हैं। 59 प्रतिशत कंपनियों ने इस टेक्नोलॉजी का उपयोग शुरू कर दिया है और 2030 तक नई स्किल्स की मांग बढ़ेगी। भारतीय कंपनियों में एआई एजेंट्स का इस्तेमाल तेजी से बढ़ने वाला है। केपीएमजी और सीआईआई की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, 93% कारोबारी लीडर्स इस टेक्नोलॉजी को अपनाना चाहते हैं और 59% कंपनियां इसका इस्तेमाल शुरू कर चुकी हैं।

articles.summary: बिहार सरकार ने आईएएस अधिकारी हरजोत कौर बम्हरा को बीपीएससी की नई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त किया। वह 29 नवंबर 2026 से पदभार संभालेंगी। एक दिन पहले उन्हें स्वैच्छिक सेवानिवृत्ति दी जाएगी। बिहार सरकार ने 1992 बैच की आईएएस अधिकारी हरजोत कौर बम्हरा को BPSC का अध्यक्ष नियुक्त किया है। हरजोत कौर बम्हरा बनीं बीपीएससी की नई अध्यक्ष, 29 नवंबर से संभालेंगी जिम्मेदारी।

articles.summary: बाहुबली विधायक अनंत सिंह की बेटी शिवांगी की शादी आज हो रही है। बारात में 151 गाड़ियों का काफिला शामिल होगा। शादी से पहले उपहारों की बारिश भी देखने को मिलेगी। Anant Singh: बाहुबली विधायक आनंद सिंह की बेटी शिवांगी की शादी आज है। 151 गाड़ियों का काफिला बारात में होगा। शादी से पहले उपहारों की बारिश भी होगी। जानें, हर अपडेट।
